analysis.title: Central bank preview: A global pause rather than an end to tightening
key_insights: Markets expect the Fed, ECB and BoJ to hold rates at their October meetings, but pricing still points to further tightening rather than an easing cycle, because energy prices and sticky underlying inflation keep restraint on the table.
Pictet's global composite central bank indicator rose to 35% at the end of September, as the cumulative balance of hikes relative to cuts across covered central banks keeps rising.
Fed funds futures imply about an 87% chance of a hold on 28 October. By December 2026 they price roughly one 25 bp hike from the current 3.75%-4.00% range to 4.00%-4.25%, then two more in 2027.
The Atlanta Fed GDP nowcast stood at 3.5% on 27 October, down from about 5% in late September. The core PCE nowcast rose to 3.15% from 3.0%. Softer growth is not weak enough to justify a cut.

US headline CPI rose to 3.74% in September from 3.40% in August. Energy contributed 1.31 percentage points, up from 1.04. Core CPI edged up to 2.56% from 2.45%, with core services the largest underlying contributor at 1.91 points.

September payrolls rose 29,000, down from 162,000 in August. Unemployment edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and August JOLTS openings fell to 7.08 million from 7.34 million. Pictet reads this as slowing hiring, not a sharp labour market deterioration.
University of Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1 in September from 51.7 in August. Five-year inflation expectations edged up to 3.4% from 3.3%, below May's 3.9%.

The US 10-year yield is pulling back from the 5.37% target and testing support at 4.93%-5.09%, which includes the rising 50-day SMA. A hold keeps the breakout intact. A break below 4.93% targets 4.81%, then the 200-day SMA near 4.53%.
EUR/USD trades below former support at 1.1325 inside a descending channel, with a downside bias driven by firmer US policy-rate expectations relative to the euro area.
OIS pricing implies about a 95% chance the ECB holds on 29 October, with the deposit rate at 2.50%. Pricing shows close to one 25 bp hike by December 2026 and roughly three by September 2027.
Euro-area headline inflation rose to 3.8% in September from 3.2% in August and 2.9% in July, while consumer confidence fell to -16.8 from -15.5. The ECB faces firmer inflation against weak demand.

France's 10-year spread to Germany is 158.5 bp, wider than Spain (66.1 bp), Portugal (52.9 bp), Italy (116.8 bp) and Greece (99.2 bp). Lagarde at the IMF meetings signalled no current intention to use the Transmission Protection Instrument for France.

The France-Germany 10-year spread has reached the extended wave 3 target at 1.54, with RSI breaking above resistance in place since 2011. Support at 1.13-1.29 holds the breakout, and a wave 5 target is 2.00.

BoJ is expected to hold on 30 October, with about 0.78 of a 25 bp hike priced for December and the first full hike priced by January 2027. Cumulative pricing is 1.65 hikes by March, 2.23 by June and 2.92 by September 2027. The meeting includes an updated Outlook Report.

The Citi Economic Surprise Index for Japan fell from 21.9 at the end of September to -8.5 on 23 October, its first negative reading since March. September exports rose 16.7% y/y against a 20.1% consensus forecast, and the trade deficit was wider than expected.
USD/JPY is capped by the 157.75-158.55 resistance cluster (200-day moving average and a Fibonacci level). A break above 158.55 targets 159.75 then 161.35-161.95. A move below 155.97 points to 152.56.

Down from 7.34 million in July, softer labour demand.
Down from 51.7 in August, widening the gap between resilient activity and household views.
Up from 3.3% in August, below May's 3.9%.
Down from about 5% in late September, still resilient.

Up from 3.2% in August and 2.9% in July, supports a restrictive ECB.
Down from -15.5 in August, a softer demand backdrop.
OIS implies about a 95% chance of a hold on 29 October and close to one hike by December.
A miss alongside a wider trade deficit pushed the Citi Economic Surprise Index negative.
First negative reading since March, less supportive of near-term BoJ tightening.

risk_factors: Persistent services inflation and elevated energy prices could force more central bank tightening than currently priced.
Weak consumer confidence and slowing hiring in the US could signal a more sustained cooling in the labour market.
Rising French sovereign risk premium (fiscal consolidation, political uncertainty, debt trajectory) could affect ECB policy transmission.
Euro-area inflation persistence set against weak household confidence complicates further ECB tightening.
Weaker Japanese data flow could reduce support for near-term BoJ tightening.

tension_points.theme: Fed tightening vs softening labour market
tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: core CPI edged up to 2.56%, the core PCE nowcast rose to 3.15%, GDP nowcast is 3.5%, and futures price about one hike by December.
tension_points.bear_case: Payrolls rose only 29,000, unemployment rose to 4.2%, JOLTS openings fell and Michigan sentiment dropped to 48.1, which could undercut the tightening still priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: September JOLTS on 3 November and the October employment report on 6 November will show whether the weak payroll month was a one-off or the start of a sustained cooling.

tension_points.bull_case: Euro-area headline inflation rose to 3.8%, supporting a restrictive ECB and about one more hike by December.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumer confidence fell to -16.8, pointing to softer demand and complicating further tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upcoming data showing whether inflation pressures are broadening or remain largely energy-led.
